import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 885

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/885](https://www.erdosproblems.com/885)
- [ErRo97] Erdős, P. and Rosenfeld, M., The factor-difference set of integers. (1997)
- [Ji99] Jiménez-Urroz, J., A note on a conjecture of Erdős and {R}osenfeld. (1999)
- [Br19] Bremner, A., On a problem of Erdős related to common factor differences. (2019)
-/

open Nat Set Finset

namespace Erdos885

/--
For integer $n \geq 1$ we define the factor difference set of $n$ by
$D(n) = \{|a-b| : n=ab\}$.
-/
def factorDifferenceSet (n : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  {d | ∃ a b : ℕ, n = a * b ∧ (d : ℤ) = |(a : ℤ) - b|}

/--
Is it true that, for every $k \geq 1$, there exist integers $N_1 < \dots < N_k$ such that
$|\cap_i D(N_i)| \geq k$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_885 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1,
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = k ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ k := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved this is true for $k=2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_2 :
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = 2 ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 2 := by
  sorry

/--
Jiménez-Urroz [Ji99] proved this for $k=3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_3 :
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = 3 ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Bremner [Br19] proved this for $k=4$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_885.variants.k_eq_4 :
    ∃ Ns : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧
      Ns.card = 4 ∧
      (⋂ n ∈ Ns, factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 4 := by
  sorry

end Erdos885

reformulations.difference: The source describes factorizations into integers, while Lean uses natural-number factors and takes their difference and absolute value in ℤ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n > 0, any integer factors a,b with ab = n have the same sign. Replacing them by |a|,|b| preserves both their product and |a-b|, yielding natural-number witnesses. Conversely, natural-number witnesses cast to integer witnesses. Natural factors are automatically positive when their product is positive. Proved the membership equivalence for every n > 0 and every natural difference d in factorDifferenceSet_integer_iff.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a finite set Ns of k positive naturals instead of an explicitly strictly increasing sequence N₁ < ⋯ < Nₖ. The three fixed-k variants use the same representation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A k-element finite set of naturals has a strictly increasing enumeration Fin k → ℕ, supplied by Finset.orderEmbOfFin, whose range is exactly Ns. Therefore positivity and the intersection of the factor-difference sets are unchanged. Conversely, the image of a strictly increasing Fin k-indexed sequence has exactly k elements and the same intersection. Proved this equivalence for every k in ordered_iff_finset, so it also applies at k = 2, 3, and 4.

review.notes: Checked the definition and all four theorems, including answer scope, positivity, distinctness, and cardinality bounds. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings. It proves finiteness of D(n) for n > 0 and of every intersection permitted by the theorem hypotheses, so Set.ncard's infinite-set default is unreachable. Boundary checks establish D(0) = univ (outside the stated problem domain), D(1) = {0}, and the k = 1 case. Independent Lean proofs verify k = 2 using {12,42}, with common differences {1,11}, and k = 3 using {112,952,3240}, with common differences {6,54,111}. The full texts of [Ji99] and [Br19] could not be retrieved; the cited problem page and Bremner's publisher abstract explicitly confirm their respective special cases. No declaration's faithfulness remains unresolved.
